crafts.boondoggle: Flat plastic lace (scoubidou, gimp, lanyard) woven stitch on stitch. Every stitch is an MxN stitch.
crafts.macrame: Cords knotted round each other or round filler cords.
crafts.chinese knotting: Decorative knots tied in one cord, shown finished and flat.
crafts.knitting: Loops of one yarn pulled through the loops of the row below.
crafts.crochet: Loops of one yarn pulled through each other with a hook.
crafts.knots: Rope knots, each with its tying steps.

entries.name: box_stitch
entries.title: Box stitch
entries.about: The basic boondoggle stitch: two strings, four ends, each folded over the next, a 2 by 2 square seen from above. It is the 1x1 MxN stitch.

entries.name: brick_stitch
entries.title: Brick stitch
entries.about: Three strings, six ends: two strings one way and one across, a 2 by 3 rectangle seen from above. It is the 2x1 MxN stitch.

entries.name: mxn_stitch
entries.title: MxN stitch
entries.about: Any boondoggle stitch: m strings one way and n the other, each from 1 to 8, left or right hand, loose or stretched.

entries.name: chinese_double_coin
entries.title: Double coin knot
entries.about: One cord, mirror-symmetric: a loop on top and one each side, eight crossings, two tails. Shown finished and flat; no tying steps yet.

entries.name: chinese_cloverleaf
entries.title: Cloverleaf knot
entries.about: Four heart-shaped leaves interlocking on one closed cord, with a stem tucked under the centre. Shown finished and flat; no tying steps yet.

entries.name: chinese_good_luck
entries.title: Good luck knot
entries.about: Three large and four small ears around a woven centre, with two tails. Shown finished and flat; no tying steps yet.

entries.name: chinese_pan_chang
entries.title: Pan Chang knot
entries.about: A square woven centre with ears round its rim, tied in one cord with two tails. Shown finished and flat; no tying steps yet.

entries.name: magic_knot
entries.title: Magic knot
entries.about: Joins a new ball of yarn to the old one: each yarn ties an overhand knot round the other. It is the fisherman's knot.
